stem: A long task with a dozen settings has to be duplicated so a near-identical variant can sit beside it in the same graph. The team would rather not retype its settings or re-wire what it waits on.

option_texts.A: Clone the task, which copies all of its configurations including upstream dependencies
option_texts.B: Export the job to JSON, edit the copy by hand, and import the whole job back
option_texts.C: Add a fresh task and point it at the same notebook, then set the rest by hand
option_texts.D: Duplicate the entire job, because a task cannot be copied inside one graph

drill_answer_short: Cloning a task copies all of its configurations, including its upstream dependencies
decision_hinge: Clone tasks to copy all the configurations of an existing task, including upstream dependencies.

plausible_options.B: would rather not retype its settings or re-wire what it waits on

eliminated_by.C: has to be duplicated so a near-identical variant can sit beside it in the same graph
eliminated_by.D: A long task with a dozen settings

distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling - a JSON round trip does copy the settings, at the cost of editing the whole job by hand
distractor_traps.C: T4: breaks a stated requirement - the settings would all be retyped
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated - a task can be cloned within its own graph

stem: Two teams each own a job, and the second must begin only once the first has finished. Neither team wants its steps copied into the other's graph, and both want to keep owning their own job.

option_texts.A: Copy the first job's steps into the second graph so one run covers the whole chain
option_texts.B: Add a Run Job step to the second graph, which is one of the available task types
option_texts.C: Have the first job write a marker file that the second one polls for on a schedule
option_texts.D: Merge both into a single job, because cross-job ordering is not expressible

drill_answer_short: Run Job is a task type, so one job can invoke another without duplicating its steps
decision_hinge: The task types available include Notebook, Python script, Python wheel, SQL, Pipeline, Dashboards, dbt, JAR, Spark Submit, Run Job, If/else, and For each.

plausible_options.C: the second must begin only once the first has finished

eliminated_by.A: Neither team wants its steps copied into the other's graph
eliminated_by.D: both want to keep owning their own job

distractor_traps.A: T4: breaks a stated requirement - copying the steps is what both teams ruled out
distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling - polling does order the work, but it reinvents a shipped task type
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated - cross-job ordering is expressible with a Run Job task

stem: A multi-task job finishes inside its window but nobody can say which step eats the time, or which steps genuinely overlap. The team wants one view that shows both of those at once before they start tuning.

option_texts.A: The matrix view, which colours each run by the state it finished in
option_texts.B: The compute event log, which records the lifecycle of the cluster behind the run
option_texts.C: The timeline view, which shows long-running tasks and how they overlap
option_texts.D: The job configuration page, which lists declared dependencies rather than real overlap

drill_answer_short: The timeline view identifies tasks taking a long time and shows dependencies and overlap
decision_hinge: Jobs have a timeline view to identify tasks that are taking a long time to complete and to understand dependencies and overlap, to help debug and optimize these jobs.

plausible_options.A: nobody can say which step eats the time

eliminated_by.B: A multi-task job finishes inside its window
eliminated_by.D: one view that shows both of those at once before they start tuning

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling - the matrix compares runs to each other rather than tasks within a run
distractor_traps.B: T2: scope error - the event log explains the compute, not the shape of the task graph
distractor_traps.D: T5: common misconception - declared dependencies are not the same as observed overlap

stem: A short-lived project is being wound up and someone proposes running the command that removes everything the bundle put into the workspace. The reviewer wants the risk stated plainly before anyone types it.

option_texts.A: It archives the deployed resources so a later deploy can restore them
option_texts.B: It removes the local project files but leaves the deployed resources running
option_texts.C: It detaches the resources from the bundle while leaving them in the workspace
option_texts.D: It permanently deletes the previously-deployed jobs, pipelines and artifacts

drill_answer_short: bundle destroy permanently deletes a bundle's previously-deployed jobs, pipelines and artifacts, and cannot be undone
decision_hinge: Destroying a bundle permanently deletes a bundle's previously-deployed jobs, pipelines, and artifacts, and this action cannot be undone.

plausible_options.C: the command that removes everything the bundle put into the workspace

eliminated_by.A: The reviewer wants the risk stated plainly before anyone types it
eliminated_by.B: A short-lived project is being wound up

distractor_traps.A: T1: fabricated - nothing is archived and the action cannot be undone
distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling - the command acts on the deployed side, not on local files
distractor_traps.C: T5: common misconception - the resources are deleted rather than merely unlinked

stem: An administrator is reasoning about how far a grant made at the very top of the hierarchy reaches. A colleague assumes anything granted there lands on every object underneath it without exception.

option_texts.A: The colleague is wrong, since most privileges at that level do not follow inheritance
option_texts.B: The colleague is right, since every privilege at that level reaches all objects below
option_texts.C: The colleague is wrong, since no privilege may be granted at that level at all
option_texts.D: The colleague is right, provided each catalog underneath opts into inheritance

drill_answer_short: One metastore-level privilege inherits down to all objects, unlike other metastore-level privileges which do not follow inheritance
decision_hinge: This privilege inherits down to all objects in the metastore, unlike other metastore-level privileges, which don't follow privilege inheritance.

plausible_options.B: how far a grant made at the very top of the hierarchy reaches

eliminated_by.C: A colleague assumes anything granted there lands on every object underneath it
eliminated_by.D: how far a grant made at the very top of the hierarchy reaches

distractor_traps.B: T5: common misconception - inheritance from the metastore level is the exception, not the rule
distractor_traps.C: T1: fabricated - privileges can be granted at that level
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated - there is no per-catalog opt-in for inheritance
